About Paralysis Recovery & Rehabilitation Therapy

Paralysis is the loss of muscle function in part or all of the body and is often accompanied by a loss of sensation. It occurs due to disruptions in the communication between the brain and muscles, typically caused by conditions affecting the nervous system. Common causes include stroke, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, multiple sclerosis, and infections like polio.

Paralysis can be classified as partial (affecting some muscles) or complete, and it can be temporary or permanent depending on the underlying cause. It is further categorized by the affected area, such as paraplegia (lower body) or quadriplegia (all four limbs).

Early diagnosis, rehabilitation, physiotherapy, and advanced treatments can significantly improve quality of life.
